html:
Rafael Carrera was a Guatemalan general who ruled Guatemala, as president and then president for life, for most of the time from 1839 until his death in 1865. He founded it as a separate republic.

A pig drover of mixed descent with no schooling, he led a peasant rising in 1837, during a cholera epidemic that priests blamed on the Liberal government. His followers, many of them Indigenous, took Guatemala City in 1838. He fought Francisco Morazán and helped break up the Central American federation.

He ruled with the Church and the old families, restoring religious orders and protecting Indigenous communal lands. In 1847 he declared Guatemala an independent republic. His rule began the long line of strongmen in Guatemala that ended only with the revolution of 1944.
